critiques.description: thr-001’s impact statement asserts that derived embeddings are disclosed to an ordinary user, but the available documentation only supports disclosure of ticket text and citation metadata, not raw embeddings or vectors.
critiques.rationale: The impact for thr-001 describes disclosure of both other workspaces’ support ticket content and their derived embeddings to an ordinary user. However, the architecture and API documentation state that the answer service returns an answer with source references for cited passages (evd-002, evd-003, evd-018, evd-026), and that answers are rendered in the help panel as plain text (evd-003). The operations notes add that the vector database is the only copy of the embeddings and is reachable only from the answer service’s network segment (evd-023). Even the candidate record describing unscoped global search says that unauthorized chunks have their chunk_id/source_ref serialized as citations, not that embeddings themselves are exposed (evd-015). None of these passages document a path by which end users can obtain embedding vectors directly. To align with the evidence policy, the impact should either drop the specific claim about user-visible embeddings or clearly mark it as an assumption/inference with rationale, focusing the documented impact on cross-workspace exposure of ticket text and associated references.
